title: Loader ring/line content-cleaning branches (map_ring_clean/map_line_clean) have zero unit coverage — every map_test fixture passes empty terrain/streets arrays
evidence: core/map.odin:185: `map_ring_clean :: proc(out: ^[dynamic][dynamic][2]f32, poly: json.Array, allocator := context.allocator) {` with branch at :194 `continue // consecutive duplicate (OSM stitch vertices)`; core/map_test.odin:157: `good := `{"board":{"w_tiles":8,"h_tiles":6},"spawn_candidates":[[1,1]],"districts":[{"name":"D","kind":"city","x":4,"y":3}],"terrain":{"water":[],"coast":[],"park":[]},"streets":{"arterial":[],"local":[]}}``. Verified: grep shows all 15 fixture occurrences use `"water":[]` (zero non-empty), and no test references map_ring_clean/map_line_clean/map_polys_load.
detail: The consecutive-duplicate dedupe, closing-repeat pop, degenerate-ring reject, malformed-pair skip (and their W4 ownership-transfer deletes) never execute in any test — only block-level fail-loud paths are pinned. The real asset exercises them only via T2 pixels, with no assertion.
recommended_fix: Add a loader test fixture with real rings/polylines: stitch-duplicate vertices, a closing-repeat point, a <3-point ring, and a malformed pair; pin cleaned point counts + the surviving geometry.

title: Saturated-estate yield (growth_board_cluster_has_room == false) never exercised — the ATTACH test cannot distinguish ATTACH from SEED spawns
evidence: core/growth.odin:739: `if board != nil && !growth_board_cluster_has_room(board, t, &gview, u32(i), cat.balance.terminal_min_sep_tiles, cat.balance.growth_groups.radius_tiles, span) {` (same call repeated at :758 in the seen-index loop). The only ATTACH test asserts `testing.expectf(t, on_pool, "attach spawn %v is NOT on a pool tile", pos)` and `testing.expectf(t, in_radius, "attach spawn %v sits outside the estate radius of every anchor (a stray)", pos)` — test_board's pool is crosses at distance 4 around the two anchors, so EVERY pool tile satisfies in_radius (radius 5): a SEED-family spawn passes all assertions.
detail: The documented interplay ('a saturated estate yields to the SEED family instead of stalling the window budget') has no pin: no test drives an estate's ring to exhaustion, and the count-loop/seen-index consistency of the has_room predicate is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Add a board test with a single-anchor pool fully consumed within the window budget; assert the run keeps spawning via the SEED family (spawn lands on a pool tile outside the exhausted ring) rather than stalling.

title: Empty-pool degenerate guard in growth_plan_demand never exercised
detail: New defensive early-return branch (skip window, zero rng draws) has no coverage; the draw-skip + rng-untouched contract it protects is unpinned.
recommended_fix: Add a test calling growth_plan_demand (or a growth-enabled run) with a hand-built zero-candidate board; assert an empty intent and an unchanged rng stream.

title: app/render/dublin.odin (even-odd rasterizer, label ordering, attribution draw) has zero unit pins — E2E T2 goldens + KYLE only
evidence: From the diff: `dublin_point_in_ring :: proc(ring: [][2]f32, x, y: f32) -> bool {` and `dublin_render_ensure :: proc(v: ^View) {`. Verified: repo-wide grep for `dublin_point_in_ring|dublin_rasterize|dublin_render_ensure|dublin_map_draw|dublin_draw` across all *_test.odin returns no matches (only map_source_test.odin references the dublin map-source enum).
detail: 445 lines of new render code are covered only at the E2E layer (dublin_board.dem T2 pixels + the KYLE gate). Matches the procedural map.odin convention, but the even-odd fill rule was the PR's own correctness-critical algorithm choice and is a cheap pure-function pin.
recommended_fix: Add a small render-side unit pin for dublin_point_in_ring (inside/outside/even-odd re-entry on a self-intersecting ring) and the label-order sort (rank desc, stable for ties).

title: Demo `map` directive parse error branches untested
detail: Happy path (`map dublin`) is covered by the dublin_board.dem golden run in CI; the two new fail-loud parse branches have no coverage. Consistent with the pre-existing harness convention (all demo parse errors are untested), hence note-level.

title: dublin_board.dem header claims district-scoped ATTACH behavior the implementation explicitly rejects — the golden does not pin district-boundary closure
evidence:
demos/dublin_board.dem:5-7: `# the user's blessed calm default) with estates clustering within districts
# (the growth_groups interplay: the ATTACH family draws from the anchor's
# district pool — a cluster never crosses a district boundary).` Contradicted by core/growth.odin:512: `// caller draws one index. The ring is GLOBAL (not district-scoped): the`.
detail: The named golden's own header documents a district-scoped attach draw that the shipped code does not implement (global ring, measured-and-rejected district scope per the PR body) and no test pins. Round-2's 'honest headers' fix missed this fixture; a reader will believe district-boundary closure is golden-pinned behavior.
recommended_fix: Rewrite the demo header to the shipped behavior: the ATTACH family draws the anchor's GLOBAL street ring (pool tiles in [min_sep, radius] of a member); the seed's district labels the estate.

title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS
detail: P0 = 100%: dual-run determinism (48 legacy demos byte-identical + dublin_board.dem T1/T2/replay), absent-when-0 map_source T1 byte, loader fail-loud table (15 paths), stride->snap->filter->dedupe pool contract, spawn-on-pool + E31 pairwise + strict-radius pins, map_source env/fallback unit pins. P1 ≈ 85%: ring/line content cleaning 0 unit coverage, saturated-estate yield unpinned, dublin renderer E2E-only. Overall ≥ 80%. CONCERNS per thresholds (P0 100%, P1 80-89%).
